name: Be decisive in ambiguity and change
definition: Find the common threads and translate vague ideas into concrete execution plans to create focus.

rows.under: Treats every signal as a new direction. Cannot say what is shared.
rows.justRight: Finds the common threads in vague or conflicting input. Names the few things that actually matter.
rows.over: Forces a single thread too early. Drops the signal that would have changed the plan.

rows.under: Leaves the idea in slogan form. Nobody knows what to build.
rows.justRight: Translates vague ideas into something a team can execute. Makes the first version concrete.
rows.over: Writes a plan so detailed that the idea can no longer change. Concrete becomes rigid.

rows.under: Keeps every option open. The team does not know what to do first.
rows.justRight: Creates focus. People know the plan, the order, and what can wait.
rows.over: Creates focus by shutting down useful questions. Focus becomes a way to shut people down.

rows.situation: Deciding while the picture is still incomplete
rows.under: Waits for certainty that will not arrive. The decision makes itself by delay.
rows.justRight: Makes the decision the work needs with the information they have. Says what would change their mind.
rows.over: Makes a hard call on a guess and treats it as settled science. Ambiguity is denied rather than managed.

rows.under: Sticks to the old plan after the facts have moved, or throws the plan out and starts from zero.
rows.justRight: Revises the execution plan when the situation changes. Keeps the team focused on the new concrete next steps.
rows.over: Changes the plan with every new slide. The team never gets a week of focus.
